source.text: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְחָמֵ֤שׁ שָׁנָה֙ יוֹתָ֣ם בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔וֹ יְרוּשָׁ֖ה בַּת־צָדֽוֹק׃

records.literal_gloss: A son of twenty and five year[s] [was] Jotham when he became king, and six-teen year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem; and [the] name of his mother [was] Jerushah daughter of Zadok.

en.L: Jotham [was] twenty-five years old when he became king, and sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem, and the name of his mother [was] Jerushah daughter of Zadok.
en.B: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.
en.R: Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. His mother was Jerushah, the daughter of Zadok.

decisions.choice: the opening of Jotham's reign: parallel to 2 Kings 15:32-33
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 15:32-33 gives the same facts. Kings first dates Jotham's accession by the reign of Pekah king of Israel; Chronicles leaves that date out, as it leaves out the northern kings' dates throughout. Here Jotham is named in the sentence where Kings says "he", the verb "was" is left unspoken, and his mother's name is spelled with a final h (Jerushah; Kings has Jerusha). The account follows directly on Uzziah's death (26:23).

decisions.choice: a son of twenty-five years: twenty-five years old
decisions.reason: The usual Hebrew way of giving someone's age.

decisions.choice: Jerushah daughter of Zadok: the queen mother
decisions.reason: Like Kings, Chronicles names the mother of each king of Judah, who held a place of honor at court. This Zadok is not otherwise known; the text does not say whether he belonged to the priestly family of that name.

decisions.choice: Jerushah
decisions.reason: The name keeps the form this verse's spelling gives; 2 Kings 15:33 is rendered Jerusha because its Hebrew spelling ends differently.

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַיָּשָׁ֜ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה כְּכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂה֙ עֻזִּיָּ֣הוּ אָבִ֔יו רַ֕ק לֹא־בָ֖א אֶל־הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֑ה וְע֥וֹד הָעָ֖ם מַשְׁחִיתִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he did the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh according to all that had done Uzziah his father; only not he went into [the] temple of Yahweh; and still the people [were] acting corruptly.

en.L: And he did the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, according to all that Uzziah his father had done; only he did not go into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And the people were still acting corruptly.
en.B: He did what was right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as his father Uzziah had done, except that he did not go into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. But the people still behaved corruptly.
en.R: He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was right, just as his father Uzziah had done. But he did not go into the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the way his father had. The people, though, still did what was wrong.

decisions.choice: did the right in the eyes of Yahweh: the verdict of 2 Kings 15:34
decisions.reason: The words of the verdict are the same as in 2 Kings 15:34: Jotham did what was right, as his father Uzziah had. Chronicles then adds the two clauses that follow, which Kings does not have.

decisions.choice: only he did not go into the temple of Yahweh: unlike Uzziah
decisions.reason: "Only" limits the comparison with his father. Uzziah, made proud by his strength, went into the temple to burn incense, which only the priests could do, and was struck with a skin disease (26:16-21). Jotham followed his father's good ways but not that one.

decisions.choice: the temple: the sanctuary building itself
decisions.reason: The word names the main hall of the temple, where the altar of incense stood and only priests could enter (26:16), not the courts where the people worshiped.

decisions.choice: the people were still acting corruptly
decisions.reason: The verb means to act ruinously or corruptly. The text does not say what the people did. 2 Kings 15:35 says at this point that the high places were not removed and the people still sacrificed and burned incense there; Chronicles sums the matter up in one word. The corruption is the people's, set against their king's faithfulness.

decisions.choice: did the right in [the] eyes of / did what was right in the sight of / did what the LORD said was right
decisions.reason: The verdict formula, as in 2 Kings 15:34.

decisions.choice: the way his father had
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the contrast that "only" points to (m2), since a new reader may not remember 26:16.

source.text: ה֗וּא בָּנָ֛ה אֶת־שַׁ֥עַר בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה הָעֶלְי֑וֹן וּבְחוֹמַ֥ת הָעֹ֛פֶל בָּנָ֖ה לָרֹֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: He built [the] gate of [the] house of Yahweh, the upper, and on [the] wall of the Ophel he built to abundance.

en.L: He built the upper gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and on the wall of the Ophel he built much.
en.B: He built the Upper Gate of the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he did much building on the wall of Ophel.
en.R: Jotham built the Upper Gate of the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He also did a great deal of building on the wall at the hill of Ophel.

decisions.choice: the upper gate of the house of Yahweh: as in 2 Kings 15:35
decisions.reason: This clause matches 2 Kings 15:35, where the gate is probably the north gate of the temple courts (Ezekiel 9:2; Jeremiah 20:2). Chronicles adds the work on the wall of Ophel.

decisions.choice: the Ophel: the ridge between the City of David and the temple
decisions.reason: The Ophel was the raised part of Jerusalem just south of the temple area, above the old City of David. Its wall was strengthened again by Manasseh (33:14), and the name comes back in Nehemiah 3:26-27.

decisions.choice: he built to abundance: he built a great deal
decisions.reason: The phrase means the amount of work was large, not that he built something called "much".

decisions.choice: Jotham; temple; the hill of Ophel
decisions.reason: Readable names Jotham for "he", says "temple" for "house" as 2 Kings 15:35 does, and calls Ophel a hill so the reader knows it is a place.

source.text: וְעָרִ֥ים בָּנָ֖ה בְּהַר־יְהוּדָ֑ה וּבֶחֳרָשִׁ֣ים בָּנָ֔ה בִּֽירָנִיּ֖וֹת וּמִגְדָּלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And cities he built in [the] hill country of Judah, and in the wooded heights he built fortresses and towers.

en.L: And cities he built in the hill country of Judah, and in the wooded areas he built fortresses and towers.
en.B: In the hill country of Judah he built cities, and in the wooded areas he put up fortresses and towers.
en.R: He built towns in the hills of Judah, and forts and lookout towers in the forests.

decisions.choice: wooded areas
decisions.reason: The word means a thicket or a wooded stretch of land, here the forested slopes on the edges of Judah's hill country, where small posts could watch the roads and the border.

decisions.choice: fortresses and towers: strongholds and watchtowers
decisions.reason: The word for fortresses is rare and found only in Chronicles (17:12, of Jehoshaphat's building). The towers would serve as lookouts and defenses. Uzziah had built towers in the same way (26:9-10); Jotham carries on his father's work. Building is one of the ways Chronicles shows a faithful king's strength.

decisions.choice: towns; lookout towers
decisions.reason: Readable says "towns", since these were small places, and "lookout towers" to show what the towers were for.

source.text: וְ֠הוּא נִלְחַ֞ם עִם־מֶ֣לֶךְ בְּנֵי־עַמּוֹן֮ וַיֶּחֱזַ֣ק עֲלֵיהֶם֒ וַיִּתְּנוּ־ל֨וֹ בְנֵֽי־עַמּ֜וֹן בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַהִ֗יא מֵאָה֙ כִּכַּר־כֶּ֔סֶף וַעֲשֶׂ֨רֶת אֲלָפִ֤ים כֹּרִים֙ חִטִּ֔ים וּשְׂעוֹרִ֖ים עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת אֲלָפִ֑ים זֹ֗את הֵשִׁ֤יבוּ לוֹ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹןסוּבַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית וְהַשְּׁלִשִֽׁית׃

records.literal_gloss: And he fought with [the] king of [the] sons of Ammon, and he was strong over them; and gave to him [the] sons of Ammon in the year the that one hundred talent[s] of silver and ten thousand cors of wheat, and barley ten thousand; this brought back to him [the] sons of Ammon also in the year the second and the third.

en.L: And he fought with the king of the sons of Ammon and prevailed over them, and the sons of Ammon gave him in that year 100 talents of silver and 10,000 cors of wheat, and of barley 10,000. This the sons of Ammon paid him also in the second year and the third.
en.B: He fought against the king of the Ammonites and defeated them. That year the Ammonites gave him {{units:about 7,500 pounds of silver|100 talents of silver}}, {{units:about 60,000 bushels|10,000 cors}} of wheat and {{units:about 60,000 bushels|10,000 cors}} of barley. The Ammonites paid him the same in the second and third years as well.
en.R: Jotham went to war against the king of the Ammonites and won. That year the Ammonites had to pay him {{units:about 7,500 pounds of silver|100 talents of silver}}, {{units:about 60,000 bushels|10,000 cors}} of wheat and {{units:about 60,000 bushels|10,000 cors}} of barley. They paid him the same amount for the next two years too.

decisions.choice: tribute from a defeated people
decisions.reason: The silver and grain were the price of defeat, paid by the Ammonites to the king of Judah. They had already paid tribute to Uzziah (26:8). A talent was a weight of about 75 pounds, and a cor a dry measure of about 6 bushels, so this was a very large payment.

decisions.choice: this they paid him also in the second year and the third: the same amount for two more years
decisions.reason: "This" refers back to the whole payment, and "brought back" is the usual word for paying what is owed. The second and third years are most naturally counted from the year of the victory. The text says nothing of later years, so the tribute may have stopped after that.

decisions.choice: barley ten thousand: ten thousand cors of barley
decisions.reason: The measure is not repeated with the barley but is understood from the wheat.

decisions.choice: the Ammonites
decisions.reason: "The sons of Ammon" is the name of the people. Literal keeps the Hebrew form; Balanced and Readable say "the Ammonites", as elsewhere in these books.

decisions.choice: 10,000 cors of barley
decisions.reason: The unit is repeated with the barley (m3) so the measure can be given in modern terms.

source.text: וַיִּתְחַזֵּ֖ק יוֹתָ֑ם כִּ֚י הֵכִ֣ין דְּרָכָ֔יו לִפְנֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And strengthened himself Jotham, because he made firm his ways before Yahweh his God.

en.L: And Jotham strengthened himself, because he made his ways firm before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.
en.B: Jotham grew strong, because he kept his ways steady before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.
en.R: Jotham became powerful because he took care to live the way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God wanted.

decisions.choice: strengthened himself: grew strong, became firmly established
decisions.reason: The verb form describes a king gaining strength and a secure hold on his kingdom, as Solomon did (1:1). The building and the victory of verses 3-5 show what that strength was.

decisions.choice: made his ways firm: kept his conduct steady and directed
decisions.reason: The verb means to set firm or to set in order. Jotham's ways, that is, the way he lived and ruled, were held on a steady course "before" Yahweh, in his sight and as answerable to him.

decisions.choice: because: faithfulness as the reason for strength
decisions.reason: Chronicles often ties a king's success to his seeking God (26:5). With Uzziah, strength led to pride and his fall (26:16); with Jotham, faithfulness is the cause of his strength, and no fall is told.

decisions.choice: took care to live the way the LORD his God wanted
decisions.reason: Readable puts "made his ways firm before" into plain words. It keeps the sense of steady, deliberate living without naming particular acts.

source.text: וְיֶתֶר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י יוֹתָ֔ם וְכָל־מִלְחֲמֹתָ֖יו וּדְרָכָ֑יו הִנָּ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֔ים עַל־סֵ֥פֶר מַלְכֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִיהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Jotham and all his wars and his ways, look, they [are] written on [the] book of [the] kings of Israel and Judah.

en.L: And the rest of the matters of Jotham, and all his wars and his ways, look, they [are] written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
en.B: The rest of the acts of Jotham, with all his wars and his ways, are written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.
en.R: Everything else Jotham did, including all his wars and the way he lived, is written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

decisions.choice: the sources formula, in Chronicles' form; parallel to 2 Kings 15:36
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 15:36 asks, "are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Judah?" Chronicles makes it a statement, adds "all his wars and his ways", and names "the book of the kings of Israel and Judah". At 16:11 the same kind of title has the names in the other order; it seems to be the same record, a fuller account that is not part of the Bible.

decisions.choice: all his wars: more than the one told
decisions.reason: Only the Ammonite war is told (verse 5). Chronicles does not repeat the attacks of Rezin and Pekah that began in Jotham's days (2 Kings 15:37); it tells of that war under Ahaz (28:5-8).

decisions.choice: look, they are written: pointing the reader to the record
decisions.reason: The pointing word draws attention to where the record can be found, as in 16:11.

decisions.choice: "look" left out; the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah (Balanced); the book of the kings of Israel and Judah (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 16:11: Balanced and Readable carry the pointing word by the plain statement, Balanced writes the source as a title, and Readable keeps it plain. "His ways" becomes "the way he lived" at Readable.

source.text: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְחָמֵ֛שׁ שָׁנָ֖ה הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: A son of twenty and five year[s] he was when he became king, and six-teen year[s] he reigned in Jerusalem.

en.L: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem.
en.B: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
en.R: He was twenty-five years old when he became king. He ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years.

decisions.choice: the verse repeats verse 1, and is kept as the Hebrew text has it
decisions.reason: This verse gives again the age and length of reign from verse 1, here with "he was" as in 2 Kings 15:33, and without the mother's name. It may close the account of the reign, framing it before the death notice, or an early copyist may have written the line twice. The Hebrew text has it, and it is translated.

decisions.choice: the same wording as 2 Kings 15:33
decisions.reason: The Hebrew matches 2 Kings 15:33 word for word in this part, so its wording is reused at each level.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יוֹתָם֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקְבְּר֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אָחָ֥ז בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And lay down Jotham with his fathers, and they buried him in [the] city of David, and reigned Ahaz his son in his place.

en.L: And Jotham lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in the City of David, and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.
en.B: Then Jotham rested with his ancestors, and they buried him in the City of David. His son Ahaz became king in his place.
en.R: Then Jotham died and was buried in the City of David. His son Ahaz became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula: he died and joined his ancestors in death.

decisions.choice: they buried him in the City of David: shorter than 2 Kings 15:38
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 15:38 says he "was buried with his fathers in the City of David his father". Chronicles says "they buried him in the City of David". Unlike his father Uzziah, who was buried apart because of his skin disease (26:23), Jotham is buried in the royal city with nothing to set him apart.

decisions.choice: Ahaz his son: the next king of Judah
decisions.reason: His reign is told in chapter 28.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula has one wording at each level. Readable says "was buried" for "they buried him"; the meaning is the same.
